name: anamne-personal-memory-v1
description: A curated personal-memory retrieval benchmark for ANAMNE. Facts span personal preferences, project/architecture decisions, technical constraints, people, and policies. Queries are labeled by type so the harness can show where exact-match search fails and semantic/hybrid recall wins. Designed to run fully local with no API key.

facts.fact: I prefer tabs over spaces for indentation in Go, but spaces in Python.
I always use pytest for Python testing, never unittest.
My preferred terminal is Alacritty with the Tokyo Night color theme.
I am based in Austin, Texas and work in US Central time.
I am allergic to peanuts.
My partner's name is Sam and our anniversary is June 14.
I drink only decaf after 2pm because caffeine wrecks my sleep.
We chose PostgreSQL over MySQL because we need concurrent writes without table-level locking.
We ship the product to production only on Fridays, after the 2pm change-freeze review.
Authentication uses opaque session tokens, not JWT, so that sessions can be revoked server-side.
The payment service is a separate microservice so that PCI compliance scope stays isolated from the main app.
We gate every risky rollout behind a LaunchDarkly feature flag.
Our primary cloud is AWS in us-east-1, with us-west-2 as the disaster-recovery region.
The web frontend is React with TypeScript; class components were banned in 2023.
The public API is rate-limited to 100 requests per minute per key.
The Stripe webhook handler must be idempotent; we key on the event id to avoid double-charging a customer.
Never run schema migrations during business hours, because the ALTER statement locks the orders table.
The legacy billing cron job runs at 3am UTC and must finish before the 4am reporting job starts.
ChromaDB embeddings are computed by a local ONNX MiniLM model, so semantic search needs no API key.
Redis is used only as a cache and is never treated as a source of truth.
Priya owns the data pipeline and reviews every database schema change.
Marcus is the on-call lead for the payments rotation.
All design decisions get reviewed by Lena before implementation starts.
Sprint planning happens every other Monday at 10am Central.
We keep dependencies pinned and bump them on the first Monday of each month.
Every pull request needs two approvals and a green CI run before it can merge.
Secrets live in AWS Secrets Manager and are never committed to git in env files.
I keep every app in dark mode.
We tried MongoDB back in 2021 but dropped it because of consistency problems.
JWT is used for the third-party partner API, which is separate from user session auth.
The documentation site is deployed continuously to Netlify on every commit to main.
Sam in accounting handles all vendor invoices.
I take handwritten notes in a paper Hobonichi planner, not a digital app.
My GitHub username is venumittapalli576.
We measure API latency on the Grafana dashboard named 'api-latency'.
Our error budget allows a 0.1% 5xx error rate before we halt deploys.
The mobile app is built in Flutter and shares no code with the web frontend.
We use Sentry for error tracking and PagerDuty for alerting.
Database backups run nightly and the restore path is tested once a month.
I like code-review feedback blunt and specific, with no compliment sandwiches.
Customer data must stay within the EU region to satisfy GDPR.
New features are A/B tested on 5% of traffic before a full rollout.
ANAMNE's fact search uses hybrid retrieval: substring plus semantic, re-ranked by ACT-R activation.
I journal every morning before I check email.
CI runs on GitHub Actions with a 20-minute timeout per job.
We never force-push to main; it is a protected branch.
Any invoice over $10,000 requires CFO sign-off.
I switched from VS Code to Neovim in 2024 and will not go back.
